name: PLAN-Boulder County

mission_quote.text: Protect and enhance Boulder County’s environment and unique character.

endorsement_process.text: 2026 endorsements were based on the combined candidate forum held with Open Boulder and Better Boulder and its PLAN-Boulder County questionnaire.

summary: A citizen-led Boulder County organization tracing its history to the 1959 Blue Line campaign. Its 2026 endorsements were based on a joint forum and its questionnaire; its published mayoral endorsements specify ranked-choice order.

name: Better Boulder

mission_quote.text: The mission of Better Boulder is to create vibrant, livable, and connected communities through land use planning and policy.

funding.text: Receives $15 membership fees and grants from non-profit organizations supporting its community-sustainability goals; board members serve unpaid. Specific grantmakers are not named on the cited page.

endorsement_process.text: The board reviewed 2026 mayoral and council questionnaires and participation in a collaborative candidate forum before endorsing.

summary: Better Boulder advocates on land use, housing, transportation and related local policies. Its volunteer board published a seven-person council slate and mayoral endorsement after questionnaires and a joint forum.

name: Open Boulder

mission_quote.text: Open Boulder advocates for pragmatic policies that are focused on local issues and improve the lives of Boulder residents.

funding.text: Solicits donations to its 501(c)(4) and separate 501(c)(3) foundation; its 2026 UCC disclosed $200 from Jan Burton and Terri Brncic as of Sept. 22. Its separately reported IEO listed $2,000 in advertising but no contributors in that report.

endorsement_process.text: The board evaluated candidates with questionnaires, a joint forum, and personal interviews.

summary: Open Boulder describes itself as a nonpartisan local-policy organization. It has a 501(c)(4) and a separate education-focused 501(c)(3) foundation; its 2026 council slate has five names and a separately registered UCC.

name: Boulder Progressives

mission_quote.text: Boulder Progressives is committed to creating a community that is welcoming, inclusive, accessible, and safe for all.

leadership.name: Jamillah Richmond
leadership.role: Board member (as described in the group's Aug. 18 and Sept. 12, 2026 releases)
leadership.note: Not listed on the group's board page as of Sept. 24, 2026; her present role is unconfirmed. Historical listing, not current leadership.

funding.text: Accepts donations; its registered 2026 UCC disclosed $2,935 in contributions from named individuals as of Sept. 24, 2026. Its separate group-wide funding was not verified.

endorsement_process.text: Its Aug. 18 release says Richmond entered after the initial endorsement process concluded; a later release says it completed her evaluation before a full endorsement. Detailed ballot/criteria are not specified in these sources.

summary: Boulder Progressives advocates on housing, transportation and social, racial, economic and environmental justice. It published a mayoral endorsement and six council endorsements for 2026 and registered a UCC to support them.

name: Sierra Club Indian Peaks Group
legal_form: Local group of Sierra Club; Sierra Club political program (group-specific legal form not established)

mission_quote.text: The mission of the Sierra Club political program is to preserve the environment through nonpartisan grassroots political action.

endorsement_process.text: The group says its political program aims to elect candidates who support environmental protection; a 2026 press release explains policy reasons for each endorsement. Questionnaire/interview details not established.

summary: The Indian Peaks Group is Sierra Club’s Boulder County local group. Its 2026 release endorses one mayoral candidate and five council candidates; a favorable “nod” to an additional ranked-choice option is not treated as a formal endorsement.

name: Boulder Area Labor Council, AFL-CIO

mission_quote.text: The council's mission is to help working families with wage, benefit and working condition and broad working family issues.

endorsement_process.text: The 2025 endorsements were announced by its Committee on Political Education (COPE); its 2026 release says it engaged and interviewed candidates.

summary: An AFL-CIO area labor council covering six Colorado counties, with roots it traces to the Louisville Labor Council around 1870. It issued ranked-choice mayoral recommendations, three council endorsements and positions on county ballot questions in September 2026.

name: Boulder Chamber
legal_form: Nonprofit business chamber; tax classification not established

mission_quote.text: To build a strong community by supporting local for-profit and non-profit businesses, advocating for a strong business environment, and sustaining economic vitality.

funding.text: Offers paid business memberships, donations and sponsorship/partner tiers; member dues published from $395/year for solopreneurs on its membership page.

endorsement_process.text: Community Affairs Council reviewed ballot measures and the Board of Directors approved positions; the Chamber explicitly states it does not endorse candidates for public office.

summary: A nonprofit regional business chamber whose policy council and board take positions on ballot measures. Its website says it does not endorse candidates, so its 2026 graph edges are ballot positions only.

name: Boulder Progressives UCC

mission_quote.text: To support candidates for the offices of Mayor and City Council - Aaron Brockett, Ryan Schuchard, Jill Grano, Sam Fuqua, Tina Marquis, Rachel Isaacson, and Jamillah Richmond.

funding.text: City report showed $2,935 contributions and $150.21 expenditures as of filing Sept. 24, 2026; contribution detail names individual donors including candidates Aaron Brockett, Jill Grano, Sam Fuqua and Christina Marquis.

summary: Boulder Progressives’ separately registered committee for candidate support. Its filed purpose lists seven candidates; the city campaign-finance report discloses its individual donors and spending.

name: Open Boulder 2026 UCC

mission_quote.text: The purpose of the UCC is to support the candidacy of Jill Grano, Benita Duran, Tara Winer, Tina Marquis, and Ryan Jamieson.

funding.text: The Sept. 22, 2026 city filing reports two $100 contributions, from Jan Burton and Terri Brncic, and no spending.

summary: The 2026 unofficial candidate committee registered by Open Boulder supports five council candidates. It is distinct from the Open Boulder independent-expenditure-only filer.

name: Open Boulder independent-expenditure-only filer

funding.text: Sept. 14 report lists a $2,000 advertising expenditure to 4 Degrees Digital; it contains no contribution ledger. The city summary shows $0 contributions for this filer as of Sept. 22.

summary: City-registered independent-expenditure-only filer under the name Open Boulder. Its disclosed advertising report does not identify a candidate; no candidate edge is inferred from that spending entry.

name: Boulder Firefighters for a Stronger Boulder

funding.text: Sept. 22 report lists $29,600.81 total contributions and $23,670.26 spending. The Boulder Association of Firefighters/IAFF Local 900 supplied $28,669.81 in cash plus $684 in-kind in that statement.

summary: A city-registered ballot committee campaigning for Ballot Question 2L. Its disclosure lists substantial support from IAFF Local 900; it is not a council-candidate endorsement organization.

name: No on 2K: Demand Fiscal Responsibility

funding.text: Sept. 22 report shows $3,436.18 contributions from Terri Brncic, KC Becker, Jan Burton, Eli Feldman, Grant Couch, Sam Weaver, and John Tayer; $201.65 expenditures.

summary: A city-registered committee whose filed name states its opposition to Ballot Issue 2K. Its officers and individual donors are reported in city campaign-finance records.

name: Vacancy to Vitality

funding.text: Sept. 22 report shows $319.06 cumulative contributions and $299.06 expenditures. The current report lists five $37.39 contributions from Doug Hamilton; earlier contributions are reflected in the previous-total line.

summary: A city ballot committee advocating for the residential vacancy excise tax, Ballot Issue 2J. Its campaign site states its YES position and the city filing names its officers.

name: Boulder Association of Firefighters, IAFF Local 900

mission_quote.text: The mission of the Boulder Association of Firefighters, IAFF Local 900, is grounded in our dedication to provide for and protect the men and women

funding.text: Union supplied $28,669.81 cash and $684 in-kind to the 2L ballot committee in its Sept. 22 city filing.

summary: IAFF Local 900 is the union for Boulder firefighters, formed in 1948. It funded the separately registered ballot committee advocating for 2L; the committee, rather than the union, has a direct ballot-position graph edge here.

name: Boulder County Democratic Socialists of America
legal_form: Local DSA chapter (specific tax status not verified)
summary: Boulder Reporting Lab lists “Boulder DSA” as a 2026 endorser of Taishya Adams, Jamillah Richmond’s campaign lists it, and the vacancy-tax campaign displays its logo among supporters of 2J. No accessible chapter-authored 2026 statement, chapter leadership list or funding disclosure was verified.

name: Run on Climate

mission_quote.text: Fighting the Climate Crisis Starts Locally

funding.text: Solicits donations; no specific campaign donor list was found on the cited page.

endorsement_process.text: The organization invites nominations for its 2026 electoral program and says it supports local candidates running on a platform of bold climate action.

summary: Run on Climate provides support to local climate-policy advocates and electoral candidates. Ryan Schuchard lists it as a 2026 endorser; an independent announcement was not verified.

name: Transform RTD
summary: Ryan Schuchard’s campaign lists Transform RTD among its 2026 organizational endorsers. The group’s legal structure, leaders, process and funding were not verified in an accessible primary source.

name: Reimagine South Boulder Recreation Advocacy Group
summary: A logo for this group appears in the organizational endorsement section of Tara Winer’s campaign page. No independent group website, legal form, board or endorsement process was verified.

name: Colorado Working Families Party
legal_form: State chapter of a political party

mission_quote.text: Our mission is to empower people, organizations, and communities to build a multiracial and feminist populist movement

funding.text: Colorado chapter solicits contributions through its official site; donor identities for a 2026 Boulder endorsement were not established.

endorsement_process.text: Its Colorado page links to an application for its endorsement; a Boulder-specific process was not verified.

summary: The Colorado chapter of the Working Families Party. Its official 2026 list endorses Taishya Adams for Boulder mayor; Jamillah Richmond, Rachel Rose Isaacson and Ryan Schuchard for council; and Yes on city measures 2J and 2L. Checked October 1, 2026; no announcement date stated.

name: New Era Colorado Action Fund
legal_form: Action fund (specific tax classification not established)

mission_quote.text: New Era Colorado Action Fund is reinventing politics for a new generation through innovative social and political action.

funding.text: The site solicits donations; no Boulder-specific 2026 donor ledger was verified.

summary: New Era Colorado Action Fund organizes young voters and has made local-candidate endorsements. Its 2025 release listed three Boulder council candidates; a 2026 Boulder slate was not located as of Sept. 24.

name: Daily Camera Editorial Board
legal_form: Newspaper editorial board (business legal form not verified)
summary: The Daily Camera editorial board endorsed four council incumbents in 2025. No board-authored 2026 Boulder municipal endorsement was verified through Sept. 24; letters from readers are not editorial-board endorsements.

name: Boulder Weekly

endorsement_process.text: Its vote guides use candidate questionnaires and publish endorsements; no detailed 2026 process was verified.

summary: Boulder Weekly publishes election guides and endorsements. Its vote-guide page reviewed here showed older guides, and no 2026 Boulder mayor/council slate was verified by Sept. 24.

name: Boulder County Democratic Party
summary: The county party publishes information about partisan county and state candidates. No 2026 City of Boulder nonpartisan mayor/council endorsement was verified on its candidate page by Sept. 24.

name: Boulder Police Officers Association
summary: City records identify the Boulder Police Officers Association as an exclusive bargaining agent for covered police employees. No municipal 2026 candidate or ballot endorsement by the association was verified.
